label: Local repair network
why_this_fixture: A physical, local, two-sided service rather than software. Tests whether a model can position something offline without falling into marketplace boilerplate ("connecting X with Y"), and whether the three lenses can find genuinely different audiences (owners, repairers, the council).

problem.statement: People throw away appliances that could be fixed because finding someone trustworthy to fix them is harder than buying new
problem.importance: A working washing machine goes to landfill over a twenty-pound part, and the owner pays for a new one

primary: Households in small towns with a broken appliance
secondary: Retired engineers and tradespeople who repair as side work
needs: Knowing whether a repair is worth it before committing money
pain_points: No way to judge whether a quote is fair
Waiting a week for someone who may not turn up
Being told it is cheaper to replace
behaviors: Default to buying new when unsure

product.description: A local network that connects people with broken appliances to vetted repairers in their town, with an upfront view of whether the repair is worth doing

assumptions: Starting in one town before expanding
